properties.name: Pegunungan Barisan (Bukit Barisan Mountain System)
properties.description: ~1,700 km long spine mountain system of Sumatra, formed by Cenozoic magmatic arc activity and oblique plate convergence along the Sunda-Java trench.
properties.rock_type: Granitoid batholiths, andesite-dacite volcanics, pre-Tertiary metamorphic basement
properties.evidence_description: Continuous high-relief fault-bounded mountain belt traversing Sumatra with dissected volcanic massifs and pull-apart basins along the Great Sumatran Fault.
properties.evidence_significance: Represents the primary morphotectonic backbone of Sumatra, illustrating magmatic arc evolution and strike-slip terrane deformation.
properties.why_it_matters: The Barisan Mountains host major active geothermal systems, mineralized plutonic complexes, and active tectonic fault grabens across Sumatra.
properties.source: Barber, Crow & Milsom (2005) 'Sumatra: Geology, Resources and Tectonic Evolution' (Geol. Soc. London Memoir 31) & Van Bemmelen (1949)
properties.geometry_note: Polygon envelope represents generalized macro-physiographic mountain province (interface visual convention, not official cadastral survey vector).
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon envelope represents generalized macro-physiographic mountain province (interface visual convention, not official cadastral survey vector).

properties.name: Pegunungan Meratus (Meratus Suture & Ophiolite Complex)
properties.description: Uplifted Cretaceous subduction-accretion complex and ophiolitic suture belt in South Kalimantan, separating the Barito and Asem-Asem basins.
properties.rock_type: Serpentinized peridotite, gabbro, pillow basalt, radiolarian chert, schist
properties.evidence_description: Exposed Mesozoic ultramafic ophiolite sequence and high-pressure blueschist metamorphic blocks thrust over continental basement.
properties.evidence_significance: Crucial suture zone marking Cretaceous collision between the Schwaner/Sundaland block and East Java-Paternoster microcontinent.
properties.why_it_matters: Exposes Earth mantle rocks and paleo-subduction mélange in Kalimantan, fundamental for SE Asian paleogeographic reconstructions.
properties.source: Sikumbang (1986) 'Geology and Tectonic History of the Meratus Complex' & Wakita et al. (1998)
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary derived from regional geological sheet mapping of Meratus ultramafic outcrop footprint.
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon boundary derived from regional geological sheet mapping of Meratus ultramafic outcrop footprint.

properties.name: Pegunungan Selatan Jawa (Southern Mountains Zone)
properties.description: Classic physiographic zone of Java established by Van Bemmelen (1949), comprising Oligo-Miocene volcanic arc formations (OAF) overlain by Miocene limestones.
properties.rock_type: Old Andesite Formation (OAF) breccia, dacitic tuff, Wonosari limestone
properties.evidence_description: Continuous uplifted plateau and rugged coastal ranges forming the southern structural flank of Java.
properties.evidence_significance: Preserves the ancient Paleogene volcanic arc before the subduction zone migrated to its modern Quaternary volcanic axis.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides key stratigraphical record of the transition from ancient volcanic arc activity to extensive carbonate platform deposition.
properties.location_province: Jawa (Jawa Barat, DIY, Jawa Tengah, Jawa Timur)
properties.source: Van Bemmelen (1949) 'The Geology of Indonesia' & Smyth et al. (2008) Geol. Soc. London Spec. Publ. 311
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary represents Van Bemmelen (1949) Southern Mountains Zone regional physiographic envelope.
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon boundary represents Van Bemmelen (1949) Southern Mountains Zone regional physiographic envelope.

properties.name: Pegunungan Kendeng (Kendeng Fold-Thrust Belt)
properties.description: East-west trending fold-and-thrust belt in Central-East Java, formed by intense Plio-Pleistocene compression of a deep marine volcaniclastic trough.
properties.rock_type: Turbiditic sandstone, marl, volcaniclastic flysch (Kerek, Kalibeng, Pucangan formations)
properties.evidence_description: Series of asymmetric anticlines, synclines, and south-verging blind thrust faults (Kendeng Thrust).
properties.evidence_significance: Demonstrates active crustal shortening and sedimentary basin inversion within the back-arc realm of Java.
properties.why_it_matters: The Kendeng Zone hosts significant onshore petroleum potential and active blind thrust seismic hazard sources in Java.
properties.source: Van Bemmelen (1949) & de Genevraye and Samuel (1972) Indonesian Petroleum Association
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary reflects the structural anticlinorium footprint between the Randublatung depression and Central volcanic depression.
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon boundary reflects the structural anticlinorium footprint between the Randublatung depression and Central volcanic depression.

properties.name: Pegunungan Maoke (Central Range of Papua)
properties.description: Parent Central Cordillera of Papua spanning ~1,300 km, formed by Neogene collision between the Indo-Australian passive margin and Pacific-Caroline oceanic arcs.
properties.rock_type: Mesozoic-Cenozoic limestone, metamorphic phyllite, porphyry intrusive complexes
properties.evidence_description: Massive alpine fold-thrust mountain belt exceeding 4,800 m elevation with remnant tropical glaciers on Puncak Jaya.
properties.evidence_significance: Prime example of active continent-arc collision orogeny producing highest topography in Australasia and giant porphyry Cu-Au deposits.
properties.why_it_matters: Contains Puncak Jaya (Carstensz Pyramid, 4,884 m) and preserves crucial tectonic records of Australian northern margin collision.
properties.source: Dow et al. (1988) 'Geology of the Irian Jaya Region' (Pusat Penelitian dan Pengembangan Geologi) & Cloos et al. (2005)
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary represents parent Central Cordillera mountain belt; Barisan Sudirman (west) and Jayawijaya (east) are documented constituent sub-ranges.
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon boundary represents parent Central Cordillera mountain belt; Barisan Sudirman (west) and Jayawijaya (east) are documented constituent sub-ranges.

properties.name: Cekungan Bandung (Bandung Volcano-Tectonic Basin)
properties.description: Quaternary volcano-tectonic intermontane depression surrounded by volcanic edifices and bounded north by Sesar Lembang, site of ancient Lake Bandung.
properties.rock_type: Lacustrine clay, tuffaceous sand, volcanic breccia, peat
properties.evidence_description: Flat basin floor (~650-700 m ASL) surrounded by steep volcanic massifs with well-documented lacustrine terrace deposits.
properties.evidence_significance: Demonstrates volcano-tectonic basin subsidence, ancient lake damming (Danau Purba Bandung), and ongoing intra-arc tectonic deformation.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides paleoenvironmental archive of prehistoric Java and critical geological context for seismic and hydrogeological risk in Bandung Raya.
properties.source: Dam et al. (1996) 'The Late Quaternary Evolution of the Bandung Basin' & Silitonga (1973/2003) Badan Geologi
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary strictly delineates the Quaternary lacustrine and volcano-tectonic depression fill, distinct from administrative groundwater (CAT) boundaries.
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon boundary strictly delineates the Quaternary lacustrine and volcano-tectonic depression fill, distinct from administrative groundwater (CAT) boundaries.

properties.name: Cekungan Barito (Barito Sedimentary Basin)
properties.description: Asymmetric Tertiary sedimentary basin in South Kalimantan bounded east by the Meratus thrust front and west by the stable Sunda Shield.
properties.rock_type: Tanjung Formation sandstone/shale, Berai limestone, Warukin coal-bearing sandstone
properties.evidence_description: Thick transgressive-regressive sedimentary sequence (up to 6,000 m) with foreland flexural geometry adjacent to Meratus.
properties.evidence_significance: Classic Indonesian hydrocarbon and coal-bearing sedimentary basin illustrating back-arc rift to foreland basin transition.
properties.why_it_matters: One of Indonesia's most thoroughly studied sedimentary basins, hosting significant energy resources and thick coal seams.
properties.source: Witts et al. (2012) 'The Barito Basin, SE Kalimantan' & Satyana et al. (1999) IPA
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary is based on geological stratigraphic pinch-out and basement structural hinge lines, not commercial oil concession blocks.
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon boundary is based on geological stratigraphic pinch-out and basement structural hinge lines, not commercial oil concession blocks.

properties.name: Karst Gunung Sewu (Gunung Sewu UNESCO Global Geopark)
properties.description: World-benchmark tropical cone karst (kegelkarst) and cockpit karst developed in Middle-Late Miocene Wonosari Formation limestones.
properties.rock_type: Wonosari Formation coral limestone, calcarenite, speleothems
properties.evidence_description: Over 40,000 conical limestone hills, thousands of sinkholes (doline/uvala), and extensive subterranean river networks and caves (Luweng Ombo, Luweng Jaran).
properties.evidence_significance: International type-locality for tropical conical karst geomorphology and Quaternary hominin habitation caves (Song Terus).
properties.why_it_matters: Designated a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2015, Gunung Sewu is a global benchmark for tropical speleology, hydrogeology, and geoheritage.
properties.source: Haryono & Day (2004) 'Landform differentiation within Gunung Sewu kegelkarst' & UNESCO Global Geopark Dossier (2015)
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary matches the contiguous Wonosari Formation limestone plateau and UNESCO Global Geopark boundary.
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon boundary matches the contiguous Wonosari Formation limestone plateau and UNESCO Global Geopark boundary.

properties.name: Palung Sunda-Jawa (Sunda-Java Subduction Trench)
properties.description: ~3,000 km oceanic subduction trench (depth 6,000-7,450 m) where the Indo-Australian oceanic plate subducts beneath the Sundaland continental plate.
properties.rock_type: Oceanic basalt, pelagic sediment, accretionary prism wedge
properties.evidence_description: Deep bathymetric V-shaped trough (>7,000 m), dipping Wadati-Benioff seismic zone, and accretionary forearc ridges (Mentawai, Enggano).
properties.evidence_significance: Primary convergent megathrust generating Indonesia's active volcanism, island arc uplift, and megathrust earthquakes/tsunamis.
properties.why_it_matters: The Sunda-Java Trench is one of Earth's most active convergent margins, driving regional plate tectonics and geohazards.
properties.location_province: Offshore Indian Ocean (Sumatra, Java, Bali, Nusa Tenggara)
properties.source: Bird (2003) 'An updated digital model of plate boundaries' & USGS Slab2 (Hayes et al., 2018)
properties.geometry_note: LineString trace digitized from authoritative global bathymetric trench axis data (Bird 2003 PB2002 dataset).
properties.geometry_notes: LineString trace digitized from authoritative global bathymetric trench axis data (Bird 2003 PB2002 dataset).

properties.name: Busur Vulkanik Sunda (Sunda Volcanic Arc Front Axis)
properties.description: Curvilinear chain of active Quaternary stratovolcanoes and magmatic arc complexes spanning Sumatra, Java, Bali, Lombok, Sumbawa, and Flores.
properties.rock_type: Calc-alkaline andesite, basaltic andesite, dacite, pyroclastic deposits
properties.evidence_description: Chain of over 100 active Quaternary volcanic centers positioned ~100-200 km above the subducting Indo-Australian slab.
properties.evidence_significance: Illustrates active subduction-induced mantle melting, crustal magma differentiation, and stratovolcano construction along Sundaland.
properties.why_it_matters: Forms the volcanic backbone of Western Indonesia, generating fertile soils, geothermal energy, and active volcanic hazards.
properties.source: Hamilton (1979) 'Tectonics of the Indonesian Region' (USGS Prof. Paper 1078) & Hall (2002)
properties.geometry_note: Representative volcanic front axis (interpretive cartographic convention connecting active volcanic centers, not an individual physical fault line).
properties.geometry_notes: Representative volcanic front axis (interpretive cartographic convention connecting active volcanic centers, not an individual physical fault line).

properties.name: Sesar Lembang (Active Fault Trace)
properties.description: Active sinistral strike-slip fault with normal component extending ~29 km north of Bandung.
properties.evidence_description: Prominent north-facing fault scarp, stream offsets, and paleoseismic trenching evidence.
properties.evidence_significance: Slip rate ~3-6 mm/yr capable of generating M6.5-7.0 seismic events near Bandung metropolitan area.
properties.why_it_matters: Key active onshore fault in West Java with well-documented morphotectonic fault scarps.
properties.source: Badan Geologi ESDM & Daryono et al. (2019)
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault trace (interface visual convention).
properties.geometry_notes: LineString representation of fault trace (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Cimandiri (Fault Zone)
properties.description: Major active oblique strike-slip fault zone extending from Pelabuhanratu Bay through Sukabumi to Padalarang.
properties.evidence_description: Morphotectonic valley linear, offset river terraces, and shallow crustal seismicity.
properties.evidence_significance: Major morphotectonic boundary separating northern Java fold belt from southern volcanic arc terrane.
properties.why_it_matters: Active fault zone responsible for periodic destructive shallow earthquakes in West Java.
properties.source: Badan Geologi ESDM
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault zone (interface visual convention).
properties.geometry_notes: LineString representation of fault zone (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Baribis (Thrust Belt Zone)
properties.description: Major back-arc thrust fault system in West-Central Java accommodating crustal shortening.
properties.evidence_description: North-verging thrust ramps, asymmetric folding, and GPS geodetic strain accumulation.
properties.evidence_significance: Accommodates back-arc shortening across Java with geodetic locking along southern Jakarta-Bogor corridor.
properties.why_it_matters: Critical active tectonic structure representing back-arc seismic hazard in northern Java.
properties.source: Badan Geologi ESDM & Koulali et al. (2017)
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of thrust zone (interface visual convention).
properties.geometry_notes: LineString representation of thrust zone (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Opak (Bantul Fault Zone)
properties.description: Active strike-slip fault zone along Opak river graben, source zone of 2006 Yogyakarta earthquake.
properties.rock_type: Alluvium, Merapi volcanic ash, Tertiary limestone basement
properties.evidence_description: Linear morphotectonic graben boundary and persistent shallow micro-seismicity.
properties.evidence_significance: Active crustal fault controlling intra-arc basin development and seismic hazard in Yogyakarta.
properties.why_it_matters: Site of the devastating 2006 Mw 6.3 Yogyakarta earthquake.
properties.source: PVMBG ESDM & USGS
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault trace (interface visual convention).
properties.geometry_notes: LineString representation of fault trace (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Besar Sumatra (Semangko Segment)
properties.description: Southernmost segment of Great Sumatran Fault entering Semangko Bay, accommodating oblique convergence.
properties.evidence_description: Prominent graben valley, strike-slip fault scarps, and geothermal spring alignments.
properties.evidence_significance: Key dextral strike-slip transform accommodating partitioned oblique subduction shear along Sumatra.
properties.why_it_matters: Demonstrates trench-parallel slip partitioning in oblique convergent margins.
properties.source: Badan Geologi ESDM & Sieh and Natawidjaja (2000)
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault segment (interface visual convention).
properties.geometry_notes: LineString representation of fault segment (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Sorong (Fault System)
properties.description: Major left-lateral transform fault zone in Eastern Indonesia, accommodating Pacific-Australian plate motion.
properties.evidence_description: Transpressional ridges, pull-apart basins, and displaced continental fragments.
properties.evidence_significance: Key strike-slip structure transporting continental fragments from Australia/PNG westward into the Banda arc region.
properties.why_it_matters: Demonstrates rapid strike-slip terrane transport shaping Eastern Indonesia's complex tectonic mosaic.
properties.source: Badan Geologi ESDM & USGS
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault system (interface visual convention).
properties.geometry_notes: LineString representation of fault system (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Kompleks Melange Ciletuh (Subduction Complex)
properties.description: Pre-Tertiary subduction melange complex exposed at Ciletuh, West Java, featuring chaotic blocks of ophiolite, metamorphic schists, and deep-marine sediments.
properties.evidence_description: Exposed tectonic mélange blocks comprising oceanic crustal rocks embedded in sheared matrix.
properties.evidence_significance: Provides direct petrological evidence of ancient Cretaceous subduction accretion along Sundaland.
properties.why_it_matters: Ciletuh exposes Java's oldest basement rocks, allowing geoscientists to reconstruct Cretaceous plate subduction history.
properties.source: UNESCO Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu Geopark & Badan Geologi ESDM
properties.geometry_note: Polygon representation of complex boundary (interface visual convention).
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon representation of complex boundary (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Kompleks Melange Karangsambung (Ophiolite Complex)
properties.description: Cretaceous subduction accretionary complex exposing ophiolite sequence, pillow basalts, red chert, and tectonic melange in Kebumen, Central Java.
properties.rock_type: Pillow Basalt, Red Chert, Serpentinite, Mica Schist
properties.evidence_description: Deep marine pillow basalts and radiolarian chert blocks structurally chaotic in scaly clay matrix.
properties.evidence_significance: Classic Indonesian tectonic benchmark site illustrating ancient subduction zone lithologies.
properties.why_it_matters: Karangsambung serves as Indonesia's open-air geological laboratory for studying subduction zone dynamics and ophiolite emplacement.
properties.source: Balai Informasi Geologi Karangsambung & Badan Geologi ESDM
properties.geometry_note: Polygon representation of complex boundary (interface visual convention).
properties.geometry_notes: Polygon representation of complex boundary (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Ngandong Homo erectus (Solo Man) Site
properties.description: Late Pleistocene alluvial terrace locality along the Bengawan Solo River where 14 Homo erectus (Solo Man) calvaria and tibia were discovered between 1931 and 1933.
properties.discovery_locality: Bengawan Solo High Terrace, Ngandong, Blora
properties.fossil_material: 14 cranial calvaria, tibia fragments, Stegodon & Bubalus fossils
properties.paleoenvironment: Open-woodland riverine terrace and seasonal floodplain
properties.evidence_description: Fossilized cranial and tibial remains of Homo erectus discovered within stratified terrace sand and gravel beds of the High Terrace of Bengawan Solo.
properties.evidence_significance: Stratified cranial elements confirm the survival of late Homo erectus in Java until the late Middle-to-Late Pleistocene transition.
properties.why_it_matters: Ngandong represents the youngest globally documented population of Homo erectus, providing critical chronological constraints on hominin survival in Southeast Asia.
properties.source: Tier 3: Widianto (2006, 2024), Berkala Arkeologi / BRIN / Rizal et al. (2020) Nature 577:381
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates verified from BRIN archaeological benchmark maps for the Ngandong Bengawan Solo high terrace excavation pit (7.2185° S, 111.4319° E).
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates verified from BRIN archaeological benchmark maps for the Ngandong Bengawan Solo high terrace excavation pit (7.2185° S, 111.4319° E).

properties.name: Perning (Mojokerto) Homo erectus Child Site
properties.description: Early Pleistocene volcanic-alluvial site in Jetis, Mojokerto, famous for the 1936 discovery of the juvenile Pithecanthropus mojokertensis (Mojokerto child) skull.
properties.discovery_locality: Sumberrame / Perning, Jetis, Mojokerto
properties.paleoenvironment: Volcanic deltaic mudflat & river channel floodplain
properties.evidence_description: Calvaria of a young hominin child recovered from tuffaceous sandstone beds of the lower Pucangan (Mojokerto) Formation.
properties.evidence_significance: Provides direct fossil evidence for the earliest hominin colonization of Sundaland during the Early Pleistocene.
properties.why_it_matters: One of the oldest hominin specimens in Southeast Asia (~1.8 Ma), demonstrating early hominin adaptability across tropical volcanic delta environments.
properties.source: Tier 3: Huffman et al. (2006) Journal of Human Evolution / Swisher et al. (1994) Science
properties.geometry_notes: Discovery locality verified via historical Geological Survey of Indonesia benchmarks and published stratigraphy in Sumberrame/Perning.
properties.geometry_note: Discovery locality verified via historical Geological Survey of Indonesia benchmarks and published stratigraphy in Sumberrame/Perning.

properties.name: Sambungmacan Progressive Homo erectus Site
properties.description: Bengawan Solo river canal shortcut locality in Sragen where morphologically progressive Homo erectus crania (Sm 1, Sm 3, Sm 4) were recovered.
properties.discovery_locality: Sambungmacan Canal Cut, Sragen, Central Java
properties.fossil_material: Sm 1, Sm 3, Sm 4 crania, postcranial elements
properties.paleoenvironment: Dynamic river channel cut and alluvial terrace
properties.evidence_description: Multiple well-preserved Homo erectus calvaria recovered during canal excavations through fluvial gravels of the ancient Solo River.
properties.evidence_significance: Intermediate cranial capacity and cranial vault contour demonstrate progressive morphological transition between classic Sangiran and Ngandong hominins.
properties.why_it_matters: Fills a key morphological and chronological gap in Javanese human evolution, linking early Pleistocene Homo erectus to late Pleistocene forms.
properties.source: Tier 3: Delson et al. (2001) Anat Rec / Baba et al. (2003) Science / BRIN Arkeologi
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates anchored to the Sambungmacan canal cutoff excavation site along the Bengawan Solo meander in Sragen Regency.
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates anchored to the Sambungmacan canal cutoff excavation site along the Bengawan Solo meander in Sragen Regency.

properties.name: Ngawi (Selopuro) Homo erectus Skull Site
properties.description: Bengawan Solo riverbank site at Selopuro, Ngawi, where an exceptionally complete adult Homo erectus cranium (Ngawi 1) was discovered in 1987.
properties.discovery_locality: Selopuro gravel bend, Pitu, Ngawi, East Java
properties.paleoenvironment: Meandering river terrace gravel bar and floodplain
properties.evidence_description: Intact Homo erectus skull specimen (Ngawi 1) recovered from basal gravels of the lower Bengawan Solo terrace system.
properties.evidence_significance: Undeformed cranial base and vault geometry provide precise metric data on late Javanese Homo erectus cranial architecture.
properties.why_it_matters: One of the best-preserved adult Homo erectus crania discovered in Java, showing affinities with the late Ngandong morphotype.
properties.source: Tier 3: Sartono (1991) / Widianto & Zeitoun (2003) C. R. Palevol 2:163
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates tied directly to the Selopuro river bend gravel deposits in Pitu District, Ngawi Regency.
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates tied directly to the Selopuro river bend gravel deposits in Pitu District, Ngawi Regency.

properties.name: Kedungbrubus Dubois Type Locality & Mandible Site
properties.description: Historical 1890 Eugène Dubois excavation locality in the Kendeng Zone where the very first hominin fragment in Java (a juvenile mandible) was found alongside the classic Kedungbrubus mammal fauna.
properties.taxon_name: Homo erectus / Kedungbrubus Fauna Type Assemblage
properties.discovery_locality: Kedungbrubus Valley, Pilangkenceng, Madiun, East Java
properties.fossil_material: Kedungbrubus 1 mandible fragment, Stegodon, Tapirus, and Hexaprotodon fossils
properties.paleoenvironment: Kendeng intermontane river valley & open savanna
properties.evidence_description: Juvenile mandibular fragment (Kedungbrubus 1) and rich vertebrate faunal assemblage collected from Kendeng sandstones.
properties.evidence_significance: Historical evidence marking the very first recognition of fossil hominin remains in Indonesia by Dubois in 1890.
properties.why_it_matters: Historic foundational site for Indonesian paleoanthropology, establishing the type locality for the classic Middle Pleistocene Kedungbrubus Faunal Stage.
properties.source: Tier 3: Dubois (1891) / van den Bergh (1999) Scripta Geologica / Naturalis Museum
properties.geometry_notes: General Kedungbrubus reservoir valley location is well documented, but exact 1890 Dubois excavation pit retains minor field coordinate uncertainty (~500m radius).
properties.geometry_note: General Kedungbrubus reservoir valley location is well documented, but exact 1890 Dubois excavation pit retains minor field coordinate uncertainty (~500m radius).

properties.name: Wajak Cave Early Modern Human (Homo sapiens) Site
properties.description: Karst cave site in the Southern Mountains near Tulungagung where B.D. van Rietschoten and Eugène Dubois discovered Early Modern Human skulls (Homo wajakensis) in 1888–1889.
properties.geological_age: Late Pleistocene to Early Holocene (~37,000 - 28,000 BP)
properties.discovery_locality: Gua Wajak, Campurdarat, Tulungagung, East Java
properties.fossil_material: Wajak 1 and Wajak 2 crania, maxilla, and associated mammalian fauna
properties.paleoenvironment: Karst cave shelter and tropical woodland
properties.evidence_description: Fossilized human skulls showing anatomically modern cranial traits with robust Australomelanesian morphological affinities.
properties.evidence_significance: Direct fossil evidence for Early Modern Human (Homo sapiens) occupation of the Sunda Peninsula during the Late Pleistocene.
properties.why_it_matters: Wajak is Indonesia's first scientifically described modern human fossil site, essential for understanding late Quaternary human dispersal into Wallacea and Sahul.
properties.source: Tier 3: Storm et al. (2013) Journal of Human Evolution 64:356 / BRIN Arkeologi
properties.geometry_notes: Gua Wajak cave entrance coordinates confirmed via BRIN archaeological survey reports and East Java cultural heritage registry.
properties.geometry_note: Gua Wajak cave entrance coordinates confirmed via BRIN archaeological survey reports and East Java cultural heritage registry.

properties.name: Patiayam Muria Stegodon & Megafauna Site
properties.description: Extensive Pleistocene volcanic-fluvial dome deposit on the slopes of Mount Muria containing thousands of Stegodon fossils, proboscidean megafauna, and hominin teeth.
properties.discovery_locality: Patiayam Dome, Jekulo, Kudus, Central Java
properties.fossil_material: Over 8,000 vertebrate fossils: Stegodon tusks/molars, Elephas, Rhinoceros, hominin teeth
properties.paleoenvironment: Volcanic piedmont lake basin, swamps, and savanna grasslands
properties.evidence_description: Massive accumulation of stratified Pleistocene megafauna bones and isolated hominin premolar/molar fossils in tuffaceous sandstones.
properties.evidence_significance: Demonstrates rich insular mammal biodiversity and co-occurring hominin presence around the isolated Muria volcanic island.
properties.why_it_matters: Patiayam preserves one of Java's richest vertebrate fossil assemblages, providing crucial evidence on island biogeography and ancient megafaunal ecology.
properties.source: Tier 3: Zaim et al. (2012) ITB Journal of Science / Situs Museum Patiayam / Balai Arkeologi Yogyakarta
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates anchor to the core Patiayam Museum & primary excavation ridge in Terban, Jekulo, Kudus.
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates anchor to the core Patiayam Museum & primary excavation ridge in Terban, Jekulo, Kudus.

properties.name: Punung Karst Rainforest Fauna & Homo sapiens Caves
properties.description: Gunung Sewu karst cave system (Song Terus & Song Gupuh) near Punung, yielding the type Late Pleistocene humid rainforest Punung Fauna and early modern human remains.
properties.discovery_locality: Song Terus & Song Gupuh Caves, Punung, Pacitan, East Java
properties.fossil_material: Orangutan (Pongo), gibbon, sun bear fossils, and early human burials
properties.paleoenvironment: Humid tropical evergreen rainforest and rugged karst valleys
properties.evidence_description: Fossil teeth of rainforest mammals (Pongo, Helarctos) and stratified modern human skeletal remains recovered from deep cave breccia.
properties.evidence_significance: Documents the environmental transition from open woodland to humid rainforest, marking the appearance of rainforest-adapted Homo sapiens in Java.
properties.why_it_matters: Punung is the type locality of the Late Pleistocene rainforest Punung Fauna (~128 ka), establishing a crucial ecological boundary in Southeast Asian prehistory.
properties.source: Tier 3: Simanjuntak et al. (2004) / Sémah et al. (2004) Courier Forschungsinstitut Senckenberg / BRIN
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates verified from Song Terus cave entrance benchmark in Punung District, Pacitan Regency.
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates verified from Song Terus cave entrance benchmark in Punung District, Pacitan Regency.

properties.name: Semedo Homo erectus & Megafauna Outcrop
properties.description: Multi-category Early-Middle Pleistocene site in Tegal containing Homo erectus fossils, 1,331 terrestrial vertebrate fossil pieces (Stegodon, Gigantopithecus), and 207 marine invertebrate fossils in one combined outcrop.
properties.discovery_locality: Semedo Hills, Kedungbanteng, Tegal, Central Java
properties.fossil_material: Homo erectus calvaria/mandible, 1,331 vertebrate fossils (Stegodon, Hippopotamus, Gigantopithecus), 207 invertebrate fossils
properties.paleoenvironment: Regressive coastal delta transitioning into savanna river plains
properties.evidence_description: Extensive stratigraphic exposure preserving marine mollusks in lower beds and abundant land megafauna with hominin remains in upper beds.
properties.evidence_significance: Dual significance: records a complete ecological turnover from shallow marine bay to terrestrial woodland hosting early hominins and giant primates.
properties.why_it_matters: Semedo is a uniquely comprehensive site in western Central Java, bridging marine micropaleontology, Pleistocene megafauna evolution, and early human dispersal.
properties.source: Tier 3: Balai Arkeologi Yogyakarta / Widianto et al. (2015) Berkala Arkeologi / BRIN
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates anchor to the Semedo Site Museum and core discovery outcrop ridge in Kedungbanteng, Tegal Regency.
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates anchor to the Semedo Site Museum and core discovery outcrop ridge in Kedungbanteng, Tegal Regency.

properties.name: Soa Basin (Mata Menge) Flores Hominin & Dwarf Stegodon Site
properties.description: Representative discovery point within the 35x22 km Soa Basin, Flores, famous for ~700,000-year-old ancestral hominin fossils, dwarf Stegodon, Komodo dragon, and giant rat remains.
properties.taxon_name: Homo sp. (Flores hominin ancestor) / Stegodon florensis
properties.discovery_locality: Mata Menge, Soa Basin, Ngada / Flores Tengah, NTT
properties.fossil_material: Hominin mandible and teeth, dwarf Stegodon skeletons, Varanus komodoensis, Hooijeromys
properties.paleoenvironment: Volcano-tectonic lake basin, seasonal wetlands, and open grasslands
properties.evidence_description: Fossilized hominin dental and mandibular remains alongside insular dwarfed megafauna and stone tools beneath 700-ka volcanic ash fall layers.
properties.evidence_significance: Proves early hominin oceanic island colonization and extreme rapid body size reduction east of Wallace's Line prior to 700,000 BP.
properties.why_it_matters: Mata Menge reveals the direct ancestral lineage of Homo floresiensis, resolving long-standing evolutionary debates regarding hominin arrival on Flores.
properties.source: Tier 3: Brumm et al. (2016) Nature 534:249 / van den Bergh et al. (2016) Nature 534:245 / Amerta (BRIN)
properties.geometry_notes: Point represents the internationally documented Mata Menge excavation grid as the representative focal site within the broad 35x22 km Soa lacustrine basin.
properties.geometry_note: Point represents the internationally documented Mata Menge excavation grid as the representative focal site within the broad 35x22 km Soa lacustrine basin.

properties.name: Cabenge (Soppeng) Endemic Dwarf Stegodon & Suid Site
properties.description: Late Pliocene to Early Pleistocene river terrace locality in Soppeng, South Sulawesi, yielding endemic insular vertebrate fauna (dwarf Stegodon, giant suid Celebochoerus) of the Walanae Formation.
properties.geological_age: Late Pliocene to Early Pleistocene (~2.5 - 1.5 Ma)
properties.discovery_locality: Cabenge, Walanae Depression, Soppeng, South Sulawesi
properties.fossil_material: Dwarf Stegodon teeth/limbs, giant suid tusks (Celebochoerus), giant tortoise shells (Colossochelys)
properties.paleoenvironment: Ancient Wallacean island river channel and flood basin
properties.evidence_description: Dense accumulations of endemic vertebrate fossils recovered from fluviatile conglomerate and sandstone terraces of the Walanae Formation.
properties.evidence_significance: Provides primary empirical evidence for deep-time insular endemic faunal evolution and early island isolation across Wallacea.
properties.why_it_matters: Cabenge is the type locality for Sulawesi's archaic vertebrate fauna, essential for understanding island endemism and sweepstakes dispersal across deep oceanic trenches.
properties.source: Tier 3: van Heekeren (1958) / van den Bergh et al. (2009) Quaternary Science Reviews / Jurnal Walennae
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates pinned to the classic Cabenge river terrace outcrop along the Walanae river system in Soppeng Regency.
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates pinned to the classic Cabenge river terrace outcrop along the Walanae river system in Soppeng Regency.

properties.name: Sumedang (Tomo) Stegodon Tusk Discovery Site
properties.description: Early Pleistocene volcaniclastic terrace in Cihonje, Tomo, Sumedang, where ITB geologists uncovered a remarkably intact 3.3-meter pair of Stegodon tusks in 2018.
properties.discovery_locality: Cihonje Stream, Tomo, Sumedang, West Java
properties.fossil_material: Pair of 3.3-meter complete Stegodon tusks, pelvic girdle elements, molars
properties.paleoenvironment: Volcanic foot-slope river channel and flood deposit
properties.evidence_description: Exceptionally preserved 3.3-meter Stegodon tusks embedded in tuffaceous sandstone layers of the Citalang Formation.
properties.evidence_significance: Confirms the presence of large-bodied proboscideans in western Java during Early Pleistocene volcanic arc expansion.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides tangible evidence of the western Java terrestrial migration corridor for Pleistocene megafauna dispersing across the Sunda Shelf.
properties.source: Tier 3: Paleontology Laboratory ITB / Geological Engineering ITB Field Expedition (2018)
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates anchored to Cihonje stream bed excavation zone in Tomo District; precise excavation datum carries minor field tolerance.
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates anchored to Cihonje stream bed excavation zone in Tomo District; precise excavation datum carries minor field tolerance.

properties.name: Blora (Banjarejo) Kendeng Megafauna Locality
properties.description: Kendeng alluvial deposit locality in Banjarejo, Blora, reported in academic literature for isolated Stegodon and Elephas proboscidean fossil tooth discoveries.
properties.discovery_locality: Banjarejo / Sunggun, Gabus, Blora, Central Java
properties.fossil_material: Isolated proboscidean molars, tusk fragments, and limb bones
properties.paleoenvironment: Ancient Kendeng floodplain and river channel
properties.evidence_description: Surface and shallow-pit proboscidean dental and skeletal fragments catalogued in local community museum repositories.
properties.evidence_significance: Indicates continuous megafauna habitation across the northern Kendeng-Randublatung depression during the Middle-Late Pleistocene.
properties.why_it_matters: Represents an emerging secondary fossil locality within the Bengawan Solo basin, requiring further systematic stratigraphic excavation.
properties.source: Tier 3: Academic literature brief mentions / Regional Geological Survey notes
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates placed at Banjarejo village center as a candidate placeholder; precise stratigraphic pit coordinates remain unconfirmed in peer-reviewed primary literature.
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates placed at Banjarejo village center as a candidate placeholder; precise stratigraphic pit coordinates remain unconfirmed in peer-reviewed primary literature.

properties.name: Timor Triassic Cephalopod & Marine Invertebrate Beds
properties.description: Representative point for the world-famous Triassic Hallstatt limestone pelagic cephalopod and marine invertebrate fossil beds in West Timor (Baun/Bitauni area), studied internationally since 1892.
properties.discovery_locality: Baun / Bitauni / Noil Bihati, West Timor, NTT
properties.fossil_material: Pelagic Ammonites (Arcestes, Joannites), Brachiopods (Halorella), Bivalves (Daonella, Halobia)
properties.paleoenvironment: Tethyan deep pelagic carbonate seamount & open ocean basin
properties.evidence_description: Pristinely preserved pelagic ammonites, brachiopods, and thin-shelled bivalves embedded in red and grey cephalopod-bearing Hallstatt-type limestones.
properties.evidence_significance: Provides globally critical biostratigraphic index fossils correlating Gondwana margin Tethyan marine sequences across the Southern Hemisphere.
properties.why_it_matters: Timor possesses one of the world's richest and most complete Triassic pelagic marine invertebrate fossil records, documented in classic paleontological literature since 1892.
properties.source: Tier 1: Jurnal Geologi Indonesia (Pusat Survei Geologi / ESDM) & Wanner (1911, 1932)
properties.geometry_notes: Point serves as a representative area marker for the Baun-Noil Bihati Triassic limestone formation outcrop belt, not a single individual shell discovery point.
properties.geometry_note: Point serves as a representative area marker for the Baun-Noil Bihati Triassic limestone formation outcrop belt, not a single individual shell discovery point.

properties.name: Misool Middle Triassic Ammonoid & Bivalve Beds
properties.description: Middle Triassic (Anisian) marine macrofossil locality on Misool Island (Raja Ampat) yielding Beyrichites ammonites and Daonella bivalves in Keskain Formation shale-limestone beds.
properties.discovery_locality: Keskain Outcrop, Southern Misool Island, Raja Ampat, West Papua
properties.fossil_material: Beyrichites ammonites, Daonella bivalves, belemnite fragments
properties.paleoenvironment: Open marine continental shelf and slope mudflat
properties.evidence_description: Fossilized ammonoids (Beyrichites) and planktic bivalves (Daonella) preserved in dark grey mudstones and interbedded limestones.
properties.evidence_significance: Establishes Middle Triassic (Anisian) marine sedimentation on Gondwana-derived microcontinental blocks in eastern Indonesia.
properties.why_it_matters: Misool provides the most continuous and undisturbed Mesozoic marine sedimentary sequence in the Australasian region, essential for Pacific-Tethys correlation.
properties.source: Tier 1: Hasibuan (2012) Bulletin of Geological Survey / ESDM Jurnal Geologi Indonesia
properties.geometry_notes: Coordinates anchored to Keskain Formation coastal outcrop sector in Southern Misool; specific fossil bedding plane coordinates retain minor spatial range.
properties.geometry_note: Coordinates anchored to Keskain Formation coastal outcrop sector in Southern Misool; specific fossil bedding plane coordinates retain minor spatial range.

properties.name: Molucca Sea Double Subduction Collision Zone
properties.geological_process: Opposing double-vergent subduction of the Molucca Sea Plate beneath both the Sangihe Arc (west) and Halmahera Arc (east), with the central Talaud-Mayu Ridge forming an uplifted ophiolitic and melange collision complex.
properties.description: The Molucca Sea Collision Zone is the world's premier modern active example of an arc-arc collision driven by opposing double subduction. The Molucca Sea Plate is an inverted U-shaped oceanic slab being consumed simultaneously to the west beneath the Sangihe Arc and to the east beneath the Halmahera Arc. The central collision complex is exposed at the Talaud, Mayu, and Tifore islands.
properties.discovery_locality: Molucca Sea (Talaud-Mayu Ridge, Mayu & Tifore Islands)
properties.geometry_note: Representative regional boundary polygon enclosing the Molucca Sea collision complex and Talaud-Mayu deformation zone between the opposing Sangihe and Halmahera forearcs, based on Silver & Moore (1978) and Rachman et al. (2022). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Silver & Moore (1978), Journal of Geophysical Research; Rachman et al. (2022), Applied Sciences; Widiyantoro (2003), ITB Journal of Engineering and Technological Sciences
properties.evidence_description: Inverted U-shaped seismicity Benioff zones dipping both westward and eastward beneath Sangihe and Halmahera, combined with thick central melange and ophiolitic crust exposed on Mayu, Tifore, and the Talaud Islands.
properties.evidence_significance: Provides the definitive modern analog for ancient arc-arc collision sutures preserved in orogenic belts worldwide.
properties.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the complete closure of an oceanic basin in real-time, illustrating how continental crust grows through tectonic accretion and arc collision.

properties.name: Sangihe Volcanic Arc Front Axis
properties.geological_process: Magmatism generated by the westward subduction of the Molucca Sea oceanic lithosphere beneath the Sundaland-Sulawesi continental margin block.
properties.description: The Sangihe Volcanic Arc forms the active western volcanic chain of the Molucca Sea collision system. It extends ~500 km from the volcanic centers of North Sulawesi (Lokon, Mahawu, Soputan) northward across the Sangihe archipelago (including highly active stratovolcanoes Ruang, Karangetang, and Awu) towards Mindanao.
properties.discovery_locality: Minahasa volcanic highland to Sangihe-Talaud archipelago
properties.geometry_note: Representative LineString connecting primary active volcanic centers along the Sangihe arc volcanic front (Lokon, Ruang, Karangetang, Awu) to Mindanao border, based on PVMBG active volcano catalogs and Morrice et al. (1983). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Morrice et al. (1983), Journal of Volcanology and Geothermal Research; Hall & Smyth (2008), GSA Special Papers; Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG)
properties.evidence_description: Continuous chain of active calc-alkaline to high-K stratovolcanoes and subaerial volcanic islands with deep Wadati-Benioff seismic zone dipping west to depths >600 km.
properties.evidence_significance: Key volcanic arc system recording subduction-driven magma generation and volcanic hazard evolution in Northern Indonesia.
properties.why_it_matters: Hosts several of Indonesia's most frequently active hazardous volcanoes (e.g., Karangetang and Ruang) with direct tsunami and ashfall risks to coastal island populations.

properties.name: Halmahera Volcanic Arc Front Axis
properties.geological_process: Eastward subduction of the Molucca Sea Plate beneath the western margin of the Halmahera microplate (Philippine Sea Plate).
properties.description: The Halmahera Volcanic Arc constitutes the eastern active volcanic arc of the Molucca Sea collision zone. It forms a distinct ~250 km chain of volcanic islands and volcanic cones along the western arm of Halmahera Island, featuring prominent active centers such as Gamalama (Ternate), Tidore, Makian, Ibu, and Dukono.
properties.discovery_locality: Western Halmahera volcanic alignment (Ternate, Tidore, Ibu, Dukono)
properties.geometry_note: Representative LineString connecting the active Quaternary volcanic vents along western Halmahera from Makian to Dukono based on Hakim & Hall (1991), Macpherson & Hall (2002), and PVMBG records. Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Hakim & Hall (1991), Journal of Southeast Asian Earth Sciences; Macpherson & Hall (2002), Island Arc; PVMBG Active Volcano Database
properties.evidence_description: Active basaltic-andesite to dacitic stratovolcanoes and caldera islands with an eastward-dipping seismic Wadati-Benioff zone reaching depths of ~200-250 km.
properties.evidence_significance: Demonstrates the young, active eastern branch of the Molucca Sea collision zone and illustrates rapid arc magmatism development in island setting.
properties.why_it_matters: Active explosive volcanoes (Ibu, Dukono, Gamalama) require continuous hazard monitoring for North Maluku's provincial population centers and air routes.

properties.name: Banggai-Sula Microcontinent Platform
properties.geological_process: Continental rifting from northern Australian Gondwana margin in Mesozoic, westward strike-slip translation via Sorong Fault, and subsequent collision with East Sulawesi in Middle Miocene.
properties.description: The Banggai-Sula Microcontinent is an allochthonous continental fragment detached from the Australian passive margin in the Late Jurassic-Cretaceous. It was transported westward along the Sorong Fault system and collided with East Sulawesi during the Middle Miocene to Early Pliocene (~15-5 Ma), causing the major obduction of the East Sulawesi Ophiolite.
properties.discovery_locality: Banggai Islands, Peleng, Sula Islands (Taliabu, Mangole, Sanana)
properties.geometry_note: Representative terrane boundary polygon enclosing the Peleng, Banggai, Taliabu, Mangole, and Sanana continental platform, based on ESDM Marine Geological Institute surveys (Usman & Panuju 2013) and Garrard et al. (IPA 1988). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Usman & Panuju (2013), Bulletin of the Marine Geology (ESDM); Garrard et al. (1988), Proceedings Indonesian Petroleum Association (IPA); Pigram et al. (1985), Geology
properties.evidence_description: Paleozoic granitic-metamorphic continental basement unconformably overlain by Mesozoic continental-to-marine strata and Tertiary platform carbonates.
properties.evidence_significance: Crucial evidence for continental collision mechanics and the origin of exotic terranes in the complex tectonic junction of Eastern Indonesia.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides key geological framework for petroleum exploration in the Banggai Basin and understanding Sulawesi's mountainous structural evolution.

properties.name: Cyclops Mountains Obducted Ophiolite Complex
properties.geological_process: Supra-subduction zone ophiolite obduction onto the northern Australian continental margin during early Miocene arc-continent collision, followed by rapid morphotectonic uplift.
properties.description: The Cyclops Mountains (Pegunungan Cyclops) on the northern coast of Papua near Jayapura expose a complete, well-preserved ophiolite sequence comprising mantle harzburgites, dunites, serpentinites, isotropic/layered gabbros, and basaltic lavas obducted during the collision of the Pacific/Caroline intra-oceanic island arc with northern New Guinea.
properties.discovery_locality: Pegunungan Cyclops Massif, north of Lake Sentani, Jayapura
properties.geometry_note: Representative boundary polygon outlining the steep Cyclops mountain massif and ophiolite outcrop north of Lake Sentani based on Monnier et al. (1999) and Salahuddin et al. (2018). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Monnier et al. (1999), Ofioliti; Salahuddin et al. (2018), Journal of Applied Geology (UGM); Fadlin et al. (2017), Joint Convention Malang (HAGI-IAGI)
properties.evidence_description: Exposed sequence of ultramafic peridotites, pyroxenites, layered gabbros, and amphibolites with high-grade metamorphic sole rock at base of obduction thrust.
properties.evidence_significance: Documents the major Cenozoic arc-continent accretionary event that shaped the northern margin of the New Guinea landmass.
properties.why_it_matters: Forms a critical environmental watershed for the Jayapura-Sentani metropolitan basin while presenting steep landslide and debris-flow hazards during torrential rains.

properties.name: Palu-Koro Left-Lateral Strike-Slip Fault
properties.geological_process: Left-lateral strike-slip faulting accommodating rapid block rotation and northward tectonic extrusion of Central/North Sulawesi relative to the Sunda block.
properties.description: The Palu-Koro Fault is one of the most active and rapidly moving strike-slip faults in Southeast Asia, with a slip rate of ~35-45 mm/year. It cuts directly through the Palu Valley and Palu Bay into central Sulawesi. On 28 September 2018, it ruptured in a catastrophic Mw 7.5 supershear earthquake, triggering devastating tsunamis and severe soil liquefaction.
properties.discovery_locality: Palu Bay, Palu Valley, Kulawi Valley to Lake Poso intersection
properties.geometry_note: Representative LineString tracing the active Palu-Koro fault trace through Palu Bay and the intermontane pull-apart valley, based on PuSGeN / ESDM Active Fault Map (2017) and Bao et al. (Nature Geoscience 2019). Official cartographic symbology is a UI convention, not official geological symbology.
properties.source: Pusat Studi Gempa Nasional (PuSGeN) / Badan Geologi ESDM (2017); Bao et al. (2019), Nature Geoscience; Socquet et al. (2006), JGR Solid Earth
properties.evidence_description: Prominent geomorphic fault scarps, offset river channels, linear pull-apart graben valley, and well-documented 2018 surface rupture offsets exceeding 5 meters.
properties.evidence_significance: A globally benchmarked strike-slip fault illustrating persistent supershear earthquake rupture dynamics, submarine landsliding, and major soil liquefaction.
properties.why_it_matters: Direct seismic and geohazard threat to Palu City and Central Sulawesi; cross-referenced with historical hazard event haz_palu_2018.
